name: sni-rst-first-two
description: A TLS ClientHello naming the relay's cover host draws a single forged RST+ACK toward the CLIENT. The box joins the first TWO data packets of a flow and reads the server_name out of them as soon as the name is whole in what it has — and reads nothing after packet two: no reassembly beyond that window. A hello cut in two halves is caught (the name is whole within them); one cut so that the first two packets end inside the name, or one split across TLS records, passes. Daal's stock REALITY hello is one segment and is caught; op desync's presets are told apart here.
analogue: Iran's SNI filter as measured by Bock et al. (FOCI 2020), IRBlock (USENIX Sec 2025) and Niere et al. (2025): 'inspects only the first two data-carrying packets of a flow and does not perform full TCP stream reassembly' (research/intel-and-some-working-methods.md:77), 'injects RST+ACK toward the client — single-middlebox enforcement'; the blind spot for a ClientHello fragmented across TLS records is Niere et al. 2023. Model: the first two data packets joined, exact name match, a name read from an incomplete hello (stricter than a box that needs the whole record — sni-rst-stateless is that box, on one packet), one reset toward the client. Not modelled: the 2026 report that :443 is now reassembled and clean-SNI fragmented hellos are themselves classified (pooribitwise); a box with that reassembly is sni-rst, against which no split helps.
